title.narrative: Water Supply and Sanitation Reform Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The proposed Water Sector Reform Program aims to implement a series of water sector reforms in Sri Lanka by addressing vulnerabilities for improved sector performance and environmental sustainability. The policy support will contribute to resilient and sustainable water and sanitation services delivery in accordance with Strategy 2030 of the Asian Development Bank (ADB). It aligns with five operational priorities: 1 (poverty), 2 (gender equality), 3 (climate change), 4 (livable cities), and 6 (governance). The program is also aligned with ADB's country partnership strategy (CPS) for Sri Lanka, 2018-2022, which emphasizes the need to strengthen the institutional capacity of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) involved in infrastructure and utilities.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.
1.1. Cabinet of Ministers approved with immediate effect a National Water Resources Policy (NWRP) to ensure adequate procedures for equitable water allocation and fair water sharing.

1.2. To increase water safety, reduce water wastage, improve climate resilience, and ensure social inclusion, the: (i) Cabinet of Ministers approved with immediate effect a National Water Safety Policy (WSP), concurrently with MOH and CEA, requiring water service providers to identify and manage potential hazards in water supply systems to ensure the provision of safe drinking water; (ii) MWS approved with immediate effect a GESI-sensitive Water Supply Service Connection Guideline for water service providers to ensure equity in service delivery and reduce water wastage, thus increasing water availability; and (iii) the Cabinet of Ministers approved with immediate effect a revised National Drinking Water Policy to strengthen equitable investment and improve service delivery performance in different geographical areas of the country.

1.3. Resilient, socially inclusive, and gender responsive, NWSDB: (i) established an Environmental, Social, Gender, and Climate Division (ESD) in its organizational structure with the objective of ensuring integrated approaches on environmental and social safeguards, GESI, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and disaster risk management, including being the custodian of the Climate Change Roadmap (CCR) and GESI Strategy; (ii) approved a GESI Strategy to institutionalize gender equality in project and service delivery, and day-to-day operations, and a safe and empowering work environment for female staff; and (iii) approved and rolled out a (a) CCR comprising the identification of prioritized short-medium- and long-term mitigation and adaptation measures and actions to reduce the impact of climate-related impacts, and (b) Climate Change and Information Technology Plan.

Reform area: Governance, efficiency, performance, and financial sustainability of water supply operations enhanced
Outcome: NWSDB's operating ratio reduced by at least 20% (2022 baseline: 1.03) (source: NWSDB Audited Financial Statements, reporting mechanism: Audited Financial Statements)
Description: To improve its overall performance, financial sustainability, and efficiency, NWSDB approved with immediate effect a: (i) revised tripartite SCI agreement, which was entered into among NWSDB, MOF and MWS, with revised KPIs (following updated SCI guidelines issued by MOF) linked to specific NWSDB's Corporate Plan and Financial Statements aiming at (a) increasing water supply coverage and quality, (b) reducing non-revenue water and number of staff per 1000 connections, and (c) improving financial performance and operating ratio, (ii) Financial Sustainability Roadmap with financial models to facilitate financial assumptions and projections, including forecasts on (a) financial status like operating profit/(loss), (b) profitability-rate of return like return on equity and net profit margin, (c) financial leverage like debt to equity; and (d) ratios on expenditure, liquidity, and efficiency, (iii) Business Efficiency Action Plan with KPIs linked to the FSR and NWSDB's Corporate Plan, (iv) Benchmarking report and improvement plan with KPIs on (a) drinking water coverage, quality, reliability, and availability (b) non-revenue water (c) percentage of customers with 24/7 supply and metered connections, (d) collection rate, (e) grievances satisfactorily resolved, (f) sanitation coverage, (g) sewer blockages per 100km, (h) wastewater collected and treated, (i) operating cost, (j) EBITDA, (k) number of employees per 1,000 connections, (l) electricity consumption per cu.m of water sold and per cu.m of wastewater discharged, (m) percentage of female employees, and (n) fulfilment of the strategic plan, and (v) revised IT Roadmap including an Information Security Policy and an IT Disaster Recovery Plan.

Reform area: Governance, efficiency, performance, and financial sustainability of water supply operations enhanced
Outcome: NWSDB's operating ratio reduced by at least 20% (2022 baseline: 1.03) (source: NWSDB Audited Financial Statements, reporting mechanism: Audited Financial Statements)
Description: To increase transparency and ensure a rational decision-making process for investments in the drinking water sector, the MWS in consultation with NPD approved and rolled out a climate-resilient Project Appraisal and Selection Criteria Framework with: (i) key criteria analysis on (a) demographic and demand analysis, (b) availability and adequacy of water resources, (c) health and sanitation status, (d) scope of water supply / response to ensure access to safe drinking water, (e) environmental and social impact, (f) climate effects, (g) regulatory frameworks and national plans, (h) financial viability and economic benefits, (i) cross-sectoral integration, cooperation and coordination, and (j) project monitoring and evaluation plan, and (ii) Public-Private Partnerships Screening Criteria, Gender and Social Inclusion Framework, and Environmental Management Framework.

Action 3: resilient, socially inclusive, and gender responsive, NWSDB: (i) established an Environmental, Social, Gender, and Climate Division (ESD) in its organizational structure with the objective of ensuring integrated approaches on environmental and social safeguards, GESI, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and disaster risk management, including being the custodian of the Climate Change Roadmap (CCR) and GESI Strategy; (ii) approved a GESI Strategy to institutionalize gender equality in project and service delivery, and day-to-day operations, and a safe and empowering work environment for female staff; and (iii) approved and rolled out a (a) CCR comprising the identification of prioritized short-medium- and long-term mitigation and adaptation measures and actions to reduce the impact of climate-related impacts, and (b) Climate Change and Information Technology Plan.
Action 1: To increase transparency and ensure a rational decision-making process for investments in the drinking water sector, the MWS in consultation with NPD approved and rolled out a climate-resilient Project Appraisal and Selection Criteria Framework with: (i) key criteria analysis on (a) demographic and demand analysis, (b) availability and adequacy of water resources, (c) health and sanitation status, (d) scope of water supply / response to ensure access to safe drinking water, (e) environmental and social impact, (f) climate effects, (g) regulatory frameworks and national plans, (h) financial viability and economic benefits, (i) cross-sectoral integration, cooperation and coordination, and (j) project monitoring and evaluation plan, and (ii) Public-Private Partnerships Screening Criteria, Gender and Social Inclusion Framework, and Environmental Management Framework.
Action 2: To ensure NWSDB water tariffs are adequately set and revised to facilitate capital and O&M costs recovery, and debt repayment through generated revenues: (i) the Cabinet of Ministers approved with immediate effect a GESI-sensitive Water Tariff Policy, including a water tariff formula; and f (ii) NWSDB approved with immediate effect: (a) Water Tariff Guidelines; (b) Water Tariff Setting Instructions; and (c) Water Tariff Revision Implementation Roadmap.
Action 3: To improve its overall performance, financial sustainability, and efficiency, NWSDB approved with immediate effect a: (i) revised tripartite SCI agreement, which was entered into among NWSDB, MOF and MWS, with revised KPIs (following updated SCI guidelines issued by MOF) linked to specific NWSDB's Corporate Plan and Financial Statements aiming at (a) increasing water supply coverage and quality, (b) reducing non-revenue water and number of staff per 1000 connections, and (c) improving financial performance and operating ratio, (ii) Financial Sustainability Roadmap with financial models to facilitate financial assumptions and projections, including forecasts on (a) financial status like operating profit/(loss), (b) profitability-rate of return like return on equity and net profit margin, (c) financial leverage like debt to equity; and (d) ratios on expenditure, liquidity, and efficiency, (iii) Business Efficiency Action Plan with KPIs linked to the FSR and NWSDB's Corporate Plan, (iv) Benchmarking report and improvement plan with KPIs on (a) drinking water coverage, quality, reliability, and availability (b) non-revenue water (c) percentage of customers with 24/7 supply and metered connections, (d) collection rate, (e) grievances satisfactorily resolved, (f) sanitation coverage, (g) sewer blockages per 100km, (h) wastewater collected and treated, (i) operating cost, (j) EBITDA, (k) number of employees per 1,000 connections, (l) electricity consumption per cu.m of water sold and per cu.m of wastewater discharged, (m) percentage of female employees, and (n) fulfilment of the strategic plan, and (v) revised IT Roadmap including an Information Security Policy and an IT Disaster Recovery Plan.
Action 4: For increasing private sector participation, NWSDB approved with immediate effect a public-private partnerships / private sector participation strategy, framework, and roadmap, including a summary action plan to enhance environmental, social, and governance sustainability, including climate change mitigation and adaptation concepts, into its overall plans and operations.
